newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nampak cautions on full-year earnings.
newsitem.headline: Nampak cautions on full-year earnings.

text.p: Packaging group Nampak Ltd said on Monday that full year earnings earnings were likely to show little improvement over last year as volume growth continued to disappoint and margins stayed under pressure.
South African packaging group Nampak Ltd raised first half headline earnings by eight percent when it announced results earlier on Monday.

"In a highly competitive environment, packaging group Nampak increased headline earnings by eight percent to 56.1 cents per share for the half-year to March 31, 1997," the company said in a statement.
Nampak's attributable earnings climbed to 55.9 cents per share from 52.2 cents previously and the interim dividend was slightly more at 14.4 cents from 13.7 cents.
But Nampak said full year earnings were likely to show little improvement against a backdrop of weak consumer spending.
"Given current market conditions, volume growth for the remainder of the year is expected to be disappointing and pressure on margins will continue," Nampak said.

It added that actions to improve operations underperforming in the first half were expected to have some impact and interest charges were seen falling but that these benefits were unlikely to offset the decline in margins.
Nampak chairman Brian Connellan said the market has been characterised by pressures on existing volumes and a continued drive by customers to reduce packaging prices in real terms.
Connellan said sales volumes declined marginally despite some market share growth.
First half margins had been saved from depreciation charge erosion by tight expense controls and productivity gains, he added.
Financing costs were seen declining in 1997 with strong cash flows forecast to reduce the company's dependence on borrowings, the company said.
